items.title: CAS-wiring rung-0 (ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES 3D, FL-10): `symbolic ... for <var>`, bind-then-solve a single linear equation via symbolic-vm::Backend + cas-solve
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-06T23:05:12Z. User explicitly authorized adj-lang language changes ('if the language is lacking features that makes this kind of work difficult, add support to it') and confirmed proceeding autonomously ('you can make most of the decisions yourself... it's reversible'). Design researched via Explore + direct source reading before implementing: cas-solve has no public 'solve a plain linear equation, leaving other variables free' entry point (only solve_linear(a,b)/solve_linear_system(equations,variables), both requiring every non-target identifier already reduced to a number) -- so rung-0 is deliberately bind-then-solve (every parameter except the one named after `for` must already be observed). Mid-implementation the user corrected the initial design (which called cas_solve::solve_linear directly as a free function) with 'the CAS packages are not designed to be used directly, they are designed to be used through the Symbolic VM' -- confirmed via AskUserQuestion, then REDESIGNED to route through a new minimal symbolic_vm::Backend (crate::symbolic_backend::RungZeroBackend in adj-lang), mirroring macsyma-runtime's MacsymaBackend/solve_handler (the one existing example of this Backend/VM pattern in the repo), dispatching to cas_solve::solve_linear_system via symbolic_vm::VM::eval. Ships `physics/electricity.adj`'s Ohm's law both directions (existing forward `formula voltage(...)` + new `symbolic resistance_from_ohms_law(...) for resistance`). Also fixed a real pre-existing-shape bug the worked example surfaced: enforce_vocabulary's check_query only special-cased the `formulas` registry, so a `symbolic` application in any `use`/`dictionary`-scoped program was rejected as UndefinedTerm despite lowering correctly. Pre-push security review (2 rounds) found and fixed one MEDIUM: exact_rational_to_irnode's i64 narrowing accepted the i64::MIN boundary, which Frac::new/symbolic_ir::rat then negate with unchecked i64 arithmetic (overflow) -- fixed with a checked_i64 helper at both narrowing sites, regression test added, second review round clean. 14 new adj-lang unit tests + full existing suite green (247 lib tests total), clippy clean, adj_stdlib_report.py/adj_stdlib_manifest.py both exit 0. CI TOOK ~4.5 HOURS TO EVEN START on this branch (0 runs created despite `on: push: branches: ['**']` matching, across 3 pushes and a full account-wide Actions backlog drain) -- an empty retrigger commit did not help; it resolved on its own once the repo-wide backlog (from many concurrent agent sessions pushing simultaneously) fully cleared. If a future PR's checks show 'no checks reported' for an extended period even as `gh api .../actions/runs` shows the account-wide queue draining, this is now a confirmed (if unexplained) failure mode, not necessarily a code problem -- check `gh api repos/.../actions/workflows/<id>/runs?branch=<branch>` for total_count=0 to distinguish 'never triggered' from 'queued'. Rung-1 candidates (not started, all explicitly out of scope for rung-0): free (unbound) non-target variables, quadratic+/transcendental solving, and a real symbolic-identity provenance shape (StepKind::FromRewrite, currently reuses the plain formula DerivationNode::Op shape as an accepted rung-0 limitation).

items.title: Wire dyadic min/max into the plain-arithmetic surface grammar to unblock K-8 data-display formulas (e.g. range = max - min)
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-07T01:46:16Z. PR #10023's macOS `build` job initially FAILED for real (not a platform cancellation): deep_operator_spine_trips_the_nesting_guard_not_the_stack overflowed the runner's ~2 MiB worker-thread stack a few frames short of FORMULA_MAX_NODE_DEPTH's guard, because adding two more near-duplicate `if name=="max"`/`"min"` blocks (each with their own `a`/`b` ExprAst locals) alongside the pre-existing `mod` block grew expand_rec's debug-build stack frame past a margin its own doc comment already flagged as tight -- passed on Linux/Windows, not macOS. Fixed by merging mod/max/min into ONE shared dispatch block (one `a`/`b` local pair instead of three), restoring the same per-call frame footprint `mod` alone had before this branch -- no behavior change, same 252 tests green. Second CI run fully green (macos-latest build passed). This is a NEW lesson for the loop: a content-neutral change to a shared recursive dispatcher (expand_rec) can trip a stack-margin guard on ONE platform only, even when the new code's logic is correct and all local tests pass on the dev machine -- worth checking lessons.md for. Spec'd as ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES 3E (FL-11) before implementing, mirroring FL-9's exact template. Confirmed the hypothesis: RUNTIME_BUILTIN_FORMULAS gains 'max'/'min' (sorted position between floor and mod); two new `if name == "max"`/`if name == "min"` blocks in lower.rs's expand_rec, each checking args.len()==2 then mapping onto the pre-existing ExprAst::Call2(BinFn::Max/Min,...) node the latex frontend already reached -- zero new AST/engine work, no grammar change. min/max now reserved at EVERY arity (not just the one-parameter arity `agg` already reserved) since RUNTIME_BUILTIN_FORMULAS's ReservedFormulaName gate checks by name only -- this changed two existing test expectations (a_wrong_arity_call_cannot_silently_become_an_aggregation had to drop min/max from its loop since `formula min(a,b)=...` is now rejected at declaration time before ever reaching the aggregation-shadow call site it exercises; my own max_wrong_arity test had to use a non-identifier single argument `max(5)` rather than `max(a)`, since `agg` only matches a bare IDENT and would otherwise swallow the 1-arg case before it ever reached the Apply-based arity check). Shipped mathematics/data-displays.adj (range_two/range_three, MathWorld StatisticalRange.html's R=Y_N-Y_1, WebFetch-verified live before writing) as the first content library built on it, closing the ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1 'data displays' gap. New manifest objective adj.math.statistics.range (band 3-5). New e2e test formula_data_displays_e2e.rs (2 tests). adj-lang bumped 0.74.0->0.75.0. Full test suite green (252 adj-lang unit tests + all adj-lang-cli e2e), clippy clean, adj_stdlib_manifest.py (70 objectives, valid) and adj_stdlib_report.py (--fail-on-unreferenced-tests, exit 0) both clean, Python unittest suites (21 tests) green. Security review clean, no findings.

items.title: K-8 math: properties of operations (commutative, associative) as verifiable comparison formulas, using FL-8
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-08T06:03:34Z. All CI green (build macos/windows/ubuntu-latest, CI gate, CI push gate). Reprioritization pass 2026-08-07 (after FL-11/PR #10023 merged, closing out the then-current backlog): ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1 names 'operation properties' as a Major Gap for K-2/elementary math, not yet scoped or shipped. Researched fit: a universally-true LAW ('addition is commutative') doesn't naturally fit the 'relate' fact shape (which states a fact about a specific pair of concepts, e.g. deficient_in(tay_sachs, hexosaminidase_a)) or a 'table' (a lookup), but DOES fit FL-8's comparison-formula shape cleanly: compute both sides for a GIVEN instance and confirm/refute equality, citing the general law. Confirmed CmpOp::Eq / EngineCmpOp::Eq already exists and is wired (lower_cmp_op), so `==` in a formula_relation body works today, no new engine work. Scoped as mathematics/operation-properties.adj composing arithmetic.adj's sum/difference (no new formula-stdlib overlap found via grep for commutative/associative/distributive across specs/data -- only incidental comments in average.adj/data-displays.adj about `sum`'s own associative FOLD pattern, not a shipped operation-properties library): addition_is_commutative(addend_one, addend_two) = sum(a,b)==sum(b,a) (always true -- teaches BY demonstration, computing both sides independently rather than asserting); subtraction_is_commutative(minuend, subtrahend) = difference(a,b)==difference(b,a) (true only when a==b -- teaches the CONTRAST, a common early-elementary misconception target, that subtraction is NOT commutative unlike addition); addition_is_associative(a,b,c) = sum(sum(a,b),c)==sum(a,sum(b,c)) (composes sum twice, the same associative fold average.adj's mean_three/data-displays.adj's range_three already establish). Citations WebFetch-verified live before writing: MathWorld Commutative.html ('Two elements x and y of a set S are said to be commutative under a binary operation * if they satisfy x*y=y*x') and Associative.html ('Three elements x, y and z ... x*(y*z)=(x*y)*z'). Pure content PR -- no ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES spec section needed (mirrors wave2-k2-math-cardinality-comparison, not a language-capability PR like FL-8/FL-9/FL-11). Picking this up next.

items.title: Close the 'number lines' gap as a surface-vocabulary extension of greater_than/range_two, not a new abs(x) formula
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-08T06:37:13Z. All CI green (build macos/windows/ubuntu-latest, CI gate, CI push gate). RESCOPED 2026-08-08 from the original abs(x)-wiring plan (see prior note below): re-examined the citation problem and realized the LANGUAGE change was unnecessary. A number line's two elementary uses are ORDERING two positions and MEASURING the distance between two positions -- both are computations `comparison.adj`'s `greater_than` and `data-displays.adj`'s `range_two` (FL-11) ALREADY perform; a number line is a VISUAL FRAME over two already-shipped formulas, not a third computation. Confirmed no engine change needed and no new citation risk: added number-line-flavored `surface` synonyms to both dictionaries ('further right on a number line' on greater_than; 'distance between two points on a number line' on range_two) -- mirrors comparison.adj's own established discipline for `less_than` (definitionally greater_than(b,a), not a duplicated formula). Deliberately did NOT touch arithmetic.adj's `sum` dictionary for a 'jump forward on a number line' framing -- confirmed via grep that arithmetic.adj IS one of the repo's few byte-pinned libraries (has `quote ... snapshot` clauses), squarely inside the excluded_delivery_classes/excluded_scope_note territory this loop must never touch (owned by the separate concurrent CAS-provenance agent) -- so this item only covers the ordering+distance half of 'number lines', not the addition-as-jumps half. `surface` fields are decomposer-facing hints only, not engine-parsed (confirmed via grep in lower.rs: 'Used by the decomposer (surface forms)'), so no new Rust test was needed -- covered by the existing formulas' own test suites, which still pass unchanged. New manifest objective adj.math.k2.number_line (the first MULTI-library objective in the manifest, referencing both comparison.adj and data-displays.adj -- confirmed schema-valid, no existing precedent found via grep but no constraint against it either). Full validation green (72 objectives, valid; report exit 0; 21 Python unittest passed; adj-lang/-cli test suite unchanged and green). PRIOR NOTE (now superseded): Reprioritization pass 2026-08-07: ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1 names 'number lines' as a Major Gap. Researched: ExprAst::Abs / ComputeOp::Abs already exist (dimension-preserving), reachable today ONLY via the `latex "..."` `|x|` escape -- the EXACT SAME shape of gap FL-9/FL-11 closed. Citation research for a distance_on_number_line(a,b)=abs(a-b) formula was NOT clean (mathsisfun.com frames absolute value as distance-from-ZERO only; MathWorld AbsoluteValue.html's opening definition is the piecewise x*sgn(x) form; CCSS 6.NS.C.7c's clean |a-b|-as-distance framing is MIDDLE SCHOOL band, not K-2/elementary) -- this citation friction is what prompted the rescope above, which sidesteps it entirely by reusing range_two's ALREADY-VERIFIED StatisticalRange.html citation instead.

items.title: K-8 math: spatial composition (composing/decomposing shapes), derived via rule-based inference over cited primitives
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-10T07:02:25Z. All CI green (build macos/windows/ubuntu-latest x2, CI gate, CI push gate). STANDING PROVENANCE STANDARD CORRECTION 2026-08-08 (see lessons.md and memory adj-provenance-inference-standard): initially reported this item genuinely stuck -- checked 4 MathWorld pages (Hexagon, Diagonal, IsoscelesRightTriangle, Square) and none states a shape-composition fact ('two triangles make a square') as a citable sentence, since a formal reference doesn't bother spelling out something this elementary. The USER corrected the standard: byte provenance does not need to be verbatim/exact -- the goal is HUMAN-AUDITABLE reasoning. It is fine to cite primitive facts and DERIVE a composite conclusion via the engine's `rule` construct (which already exists, tested via medical-rulebook examples, e.g. contraindicated($D) derived from pregnant(present)+pregnancy_excludes($D)), as long as the inference chain stays inspectable (a query's `steps` trail shows the rule's own citation AND each premise fact's citation separately, so a human can independently verify each link and correct a bad one later) -- the same composition discipline `formula`s already use (mean_three cites sum twice, not a single 'mean of three' source). User also authorized `trust consensus` for a well-established but not-directly-source-stated derivation step, not just `trust authoritative`. Prototyped this live (rule combining the ALREADY-SHIPPED quadrilateral_property table with MathWorld Triangulation.html/PolygonDiagonal.html definitions) before committing, confirmed via the CLI that the full audit trail renders correctly (steps: kind=rule then kind=fact, each with its own citation) and that reverse-bind/abstention both work. Shipped `adj-facts-stdlib/geometry/shape-composition.adj`: rule { head: triangle_decomposition_count($Shape, 2) when: quadrilateral_property($Shape, $Property) source '...(honest split of verbatim MathWorld quote + the elementary diagonal-splits-a-quadrilateral-into-two-triangles reasoning built on it)...' locator Triangulation.html trust consensus } -- derives the fact for all 5 already-shipped named quadrilaterals (square/rectangle/rhombus/parallelogram/trapezoid), abstains honestly on a triangle (no diagonal to draw). Deliberately scoped to ONLY the quadrilateral-by-one-diagonal case (n=4 -> 2 triangles), not a general n-sided-polygon (sides-2) formula -- MathWorld states C_(n-3) triangulating diagonals for a convex n-gon but does not spell out the resulting n-2 triangle count, so generalizing further would need its own honest derivation, left for later. FIRST rule-based (not table-only) content in adj-facts-stdlib's history, and the FIRST adj-facts-stdlib-sourced manifest objective ever (all 72 prior objectives were adj-formula-stdlib-only) -- new manifest objective adj.math.k2.spatial_composition uses competency 'infer' (schema already had this value, unused until now) rather than 'recall'/'compute'. DISCOVERED AND FIXED A REAL BUG surfaced by being the first rule-based content: code/scripts/adj_stdlib_report.py's CLAUSE_PATTERNS['rules'] regex was `^\s*rule\s+[a-zA-Z_]` (copied from table/formula/relate's 'keyword then identifier' shape) but the real `rule` grammar is ANONYMOUS (`rule { head: ... }`, no name before the brace) -- so the old regex silently matched zero rule clauses, meaning source_envelope validation would have reported TRUE regardless of whether a rule was actually sourced (a false-negative gap that existed for however long `rule` has been in the grammar, just never exercised until this content). Fixed to `^\s*rule\s*\{`; added 2 regression tests (test_rule_clause_is_recognized_with_no_name_before_the_brace, test_unsourced_rule_clause_reports_missing_source_envelope) pinning both directions. This tooling fix is in code/scripts/adj_stdlib_report.py, NOT adj_stdlib_provenance.py/adj-verify (confirmed these are separate modules; report.py is this loop's own structural-completeness tool already used as its validation gate all session, not the excluded CAS-provenance system). New e2e test facts_shapecomposition_e2e.rs (3 tests: derives-with-audit-trail, runs-backward, abstains-on-non-quadrilateral). Full validation green: 73 objectives valid (was failing with 2 errors before the regex fix), report exit 0, 23 Python unittest passed (21 + 2 new), adj-lang/-cli suite green, clippy clean.
